needs.reason: build.rs is project code that Cargo compiles and runs before the crate (it runs rustc --version to emit check-cfg); rust-analyzer runs build scripts too

traps: the dependency written serde is the package serde_core, renamed: serde = { package = "serde_core", ... }; a reader that takes the key as the name says serde
a second serde entry sits under [target.'cfg(any())'.dependencies]: cfg(any()) is never true, so that dependency never builds; it only makes the published manifest name serde
criterion is a dev-dependency only for targets where cfg(not(miri)) holds
no Cargo.lock in the repository: every resolved is null
tests/util/mod.rs is not a crate: three integration-test crates include it with mod util;, so the same file is compiled three times

tests/node/mod.rs is included by test_version_req.rs with mod node; but starts with #![cfg(test_node_semver)]: it compiles only when RUSTFLAGS carries --cfg test_node_semver, which only the Node CI job sets (that job also runs npm install semver and calls node)
build.rs only declares the custom cfg test_node_semver to rustc >= 1.80 (cargo:rustc-check-cfg); it is excluded from the published package (exclude = ["build.rs"])

fuzz/ is its own crate (semver-fuzz, publish = false) with an empty [workspace] table: it is a workspace root of its own, so the root package is not a workspace and does not see fuzz/ as a member; semver-fuzz depends on semver by path = ".."
features: default = ["std"], serde = ["dep:serde"], std = []; the crate is no_std without std
besides the matrix, other CI jobs pick toolchains through action refs: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable (node, outdated), @nightly (minimal, doc, fuzz), @clippy and @miri
rust-version 1.68 and the 1.68.0 matrix entry agree; on 1.68.0 CI skips cargo test (if: matrix.rust != '1.68.0')
